characters.name: Luffy
characters.kicker: North star / favorite in all fiction
characters.body: The GOAT for me. What makes Luffy special is not just the gears, fights or ridiculous move names. It is the way he stays loyal to his morals, protects his people at any cost, keeps the same dream even when the world laughs, and keeps moving after moments that should have broken him. He also helped me loosen the grip of overthinking and enjoy the part of life that is actually happening now.
characters.note: The Wano fits and Gear 2 → Gear 5 hype are absolutely part of the case too.

characters.name: Robin
characters.kicker: Emotional core / crush in all fiction
characters.body: Yes, she is my fictional crush. But the story is why she stayed. Robin survives Ohara, years of being hunted and the belief that people will eventually abandon her. Then the Straw Hats show her the opposite: she is worth crossing the world for. Enies Lobby turns that entire life of running into one request to keep living, and that is the moment she completely stole my heart.
characters.note: For me, Robin is proof that finding the right people can change the meaning of everything that came before.

characters.name: Zoro
characters.body: Zoro does not need a giant speech every episode. His sheer will, refusal to quit and unwavering loyalty to his captain do the talking. The lesson I take from him is simple: keep aiming higher, keep going, and one day you will look back and barely recognize how far you have climbed.

characters.name: Guts
characters.body: Emotionally and psychologically, one of the strongest journeys in fiction for me. The amount of trauma and cruelty thrown at Guts is almost absurd, but the point is that suffering never gets the final word. He keeps prevailing. Also, the armor, the presence and that gigantic sword are just ridiculously cool.

characters.name: Ayanokoji
characters.body: I never expected a manipulative high-school character to land this high for me. What I actually admire is his emotional control, awareness, selective self-revelation and ability to handle complex situations without needing attention. I do not admire treating people like tools, but the composure and decision-making are areas I want to sharpen in myself.

characters.name: Subaru Natsuki
characters.kicker: Try again, even when nobody remembers
characters.body: I completely misjudged him at first. What looked like weakness became the exact reason I respected him: Subaru can be terrified, humiliated, broken and still walk back into a nightmare because the people around him matter more than his pride. Return by Death is not a cool reset button to me anymore. It is loneliness with a checkpoint.
characters.note: Biggest opinion reversal in the archive. The charges have officially been withdrawn. 😂

characters.name: All Might
characters.body: All Might works for me because of what he represents. People see him and believe help has arrived. That final stand and iconic raised fist hit harder than a long personality essay ever could. Sometimes what you symbolize to other people matters just as much as what you say.

characters.name: Rudeus
characters.body: A deeply flawed guy, but the second-chance premise left me with a very real lesson: real life does not hand us a reincarnation button. Eventually we have to stop running from our problems, accept who we are, face reality head-on and try to live without regrets.
characters.note: The three wives are not the lesson. That part is just Rudeus winning the lottery. 😭

characters.name: Sanji
characters.body: Sanji is a hardworking cook who gives his best, carries two backstories and, yes, is still a catastrophic simp. The most practical thing he left with me is respect for food: do not waste what is on the table, because there is real work and value behind every meal.

journey.title: Berserk: The Golden Age
journey.body: One of my first proper steps into anime, right after my A/Ls. I did not become an anime fan overnight, but Guts planted one idea that stayed with me: life can be brutally unfair and you can still keep moving.
journey.quote: You do not need an easy life to keep moving forward.

journey.title: One Piece
journey.body: I finished the available story in roughly three months and immediately regretted speedrunning it. Nothing felt the same afterward. Luffy turned dreaming loudly from something I found ridiculous into something I deeply respect.
journey.quote: Dream loudly. Protect your people. Keep moving.

journey.title: AOT → JJK → Demon Slayer
journey.body: This run helped me discover my personal filter. Beautiful animation can absolutely get my attention, but it cannot make me care by itself. I need the story and characters to leave something behind.
journey.quote: Pretty animation can get my attention. Emotion is what makes me stay.

journey.title: One Piece rewatch #2
journey.body: This time I watched with my sister. Suddenly I was not just revisiting scenes, I was waiting for somebody else to reach the emotional landmines while pretending to act normal. The story became part of family life too.

journey.title: Black Clover
journey.body: Asta is basically a walking refusal to accept the limit he was given. Loud? Extremely. But underneath it is something I respect: work until the impossible becomes less impossible.

journey.title: Classroom of the Elite
journey.body: Ayanokoji became one of my favorites because of awareness, composure, observation and control over what he reveals. I want the discipline, not the dehumanization.
journey.quote: Take the discipline. Leave the dehumanization.

journey.title: Re:Zero
journey.body: I started by calling Subaru a dumb simp and ended up respecting him for exactly the emotions I first mistook for weakness. Return by Death stopped looking like a power and started looking like a curse nobody else can remember.

journey.title: The Fragrant Flower Blooms with Dignity
journey.body: My first proper romance anime dismantled another assumption. The relationship felt sincere and emotionally mature enough that I went straight into the manga afterward.
journey.quote: If the story is good, the genre does not matter.

journey.title: The doors stay open.
journey.body: Mushoku Tensei, Frieren, Mob Psycho 100, Chainsaw Man, Hell's Paradise, Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You and more kept widening the range. Anime ended up teaching me to try things before judging them, which is hilarious considering how this journey began.

rewatches.title: One Piece
rewatches.body: Second watch with my sister; third with my mother, around Episode 987.

rewatches.title: Attack on Titan
rewatches.body: I still love the journey more than the ending.

rewatches.title: Classroom of the Elite
rewatches.body: Still one of my favorite surprise discoveries.
